conventions.convention: A pseudo-true parameter maximizes the expected log-likelihood under the actual data law P. Existence, uniqueness, interiority and separation are additional hypotheses.
H is the expected score derivative, without a minus sign; J is the score second moment under P. The covariance is H⁻¹JH⁻ᵀ. AC is assumed.
Fisher distance uses a symmetric positive-definite matrix and a nonempty set; it is defined by an infimum without asserting attainment.

The likelihood-ratio statistic is twice the full-minus-null optimized log-likelihood. Its limit is null squared Fisher distance minus full squared Fisher distance. Uniform expansion and tight maximizers are explicit assumptions beyond QMD.
Uniform endpoint parameters are strictly positive, sample size is at least one, and the endpoint MLE assertion is almost sure. Exp(1/θ) uses the rate parameter.
The one-sided normal test has full space R and null μ≤0, evaluated at μ=0; χ²₀ is the point mass at zero.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC, an interior full-model QMD point with positive-definite information, the stated closed local sets and local cone convergence, a uniform local quadratic likelihood expansion with Z_n ⇒ N_d(0,I), and attained tight full and null maximizers gives T_n ⇒ d_I²(I⁻¹Z,C₀) − d_I²(I⁻¹Z,C).

Under AC, IID misspecified data, a unique separated interior population maximizer, the uniform criterion law and approximate maximization, the stated differentiable score and uniform Hessian laws, zero mean finite-second-moment score, nonsingular H, and √n P_n S_hatθ_n = o_P(1), √n(hatθ_n−θ*) ⇒ N_d(0,H⁻¹JH⁻ᵀ).

For d≥1, symmetric positive-definite invertible I, z∈R^d and nonempty Euclidean-closed C, q_z(h)=zᵀh−½hᵀIh attains its maximum on C, I has a positive Euclidean coercivity constant, and sup_C q_z = ½zᵀI⁻¹z−½d_I²(I⁻¹z,C).
A pseudo-true parameter is any maximizer of M_P(θ)=E_P log p_θ(X), for the specified density family and actual probability law under the stated positivity and integrability conditions.
For IID Unif[0,θ] observations with θ>0, the endpoint MLE is X_(n) almost surely; n(θ−X_(n)) ⇒ Exp(1/θ), √n(θ−X_(n)) →_P 0, and the model is not QMD.

concerns.concern: The Statement simultaneously requires Θ to be open and C_n=√n(Θ−θ₀) to be closed. Since Θ is nonempty and affine rescaling preserves both properties, connectedness of R^d forces Θ=R^d; consequently C_n=C=R^d. The claim and its normal example remain valid, but the apparent general full-cone formulation is redundant and its actual full-space restriction is not explained.

seams_checked.note: Compared prerequisite page prose and delta/Z-estimator Statements with the sandwich argument. No stronger delta or Z-estimator result is cited; consistency and local Hessian control are proved or explicitly assumed, and the score residual has the required root-n scale.

The QMD Definition is reproduced faithfully, including its interior full-model setting. Compared the regular calibration Statement: its linear equality-null hypothesis is not applied to the half-line null. The boundary example independently checks its hypotheses.

Compared the LAN Definition and QMD-to-LAN Statement with the cone theorem. Pointwise proxy LAN is not promoted to a uniform raw log-likelihood expansion; that stronger expansion and tightness are separate explicit hypotheses.
